subject.title: Next Sprint B: model-input validation guardrails

question: Should configured model `input` values beyond text/image be invalid, valid metadata only, or valid only through an explicit override/capability contract?
rationale: Current main intentionally accepts and preserves audio/video on some config/catalog surfaces while other runtime and registry paths still treat only text/image as supported, so automation cannot safely choose strict rejection or broad acceptance.

options.title: Define contract before implementation
options.body: Recommended: choose the canonical meaning of audio/video model inputs first, then implement one aligned schema/runtime/docs/test change with migration handling if config becomes invalid.

options.title: Strictly reject unsupported inputs
options.body: Treat audio/video as invalid in configured chat model inputs and add tests, docs, and doctor migration for existing configs that now violate the contract.

options.title: Accept metadata with runtime guardrails
options.body: Keep audio/video as valid metadata but add runtime-specific selection checks, clear diagnostics, and docs that separate chat-turn input support from media-understanding or future modality metadata.

recommendation.title: Define contract before implementation
recommendation.body: Recommended: choose the canonical meaning of audio/video model inputs first, then implement one aligned schema/runtime/docs/test change with migration handling if config becomes invalid.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans provider/config public API and runtime routing, and history shows adjacent ownership on the relevant schema and provider-catalog surfaces.
